With `root>plain` currently `position: static`, the absolutely positioned `root>plain>pin` uses the nearest positioned ancestor, which is `root` (`position: relative`). That’s why the pin ends up at `(10, 10)` (its `top: 10px; left: 10px` measured from `root`’s origin).

After adding `position: relative` to `root>plain`, `root>plain` becomes the containing block for the absolute positioning. Since `root>plain`’s bounding box starts at `(20, 20)`, the pin’s `left: 10px; top: 10px` move it to `(20+10, 20+10)`.
